path: Filtration and the finite model property

uses: Soundness and completeness of normal modal logics

results.title: Subformulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The finite set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of a modal formula $\varphi$, including $\varphi$ itself, is defined by recursion: $\mathrm{sub}(p) = \{p\}$ for an atom $p$, $\mathrm{sub}(\bot) = \{\bot\}$, $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi \to \psi) = \{\varphi \to \psi\} \cup \mathrm{sub}(\varphi) \cup \mathrm{sub}(\psi)$, and $\mathrm{sub}(\Box\varphi) = \{\Box\varphi\} \cup \mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$.

results.title: The subformula relation is transitive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $\psi$ is a subformula of a modal formula $\varphi$, then every subformula of $\psi$ is a subformula of $\varphi$.

results.title: Finite Kripke model on sets of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $U$ be a nonempty finite set of finite sets of formulas and $R$ a finite set of pairs of finite sets of formulas. The Kripke model on $U$ with relation $R$ has the elements of $U$ as worlds, a world $s$ sees a world $t$ iff $(s, t) \in R$, and an atom $p$ is true at $s$ iff $p \in s$.

results.title: Boolean evaluation in a finite model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a finite set $U$ of finite sets of formulas, a finite set $R$ of pairs of such sets and a finite set $s$ of formulas, the Boolean value of a formula at $s$ is defined by recursion on the formula: an atom $p$ is true iff $p \in s$; $\bot$ is false; $\varphi \to \psi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is false or $\psi$ is true at $s$; and $\Box\varphi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is true at every $t \in U$ with $(s, t) \in R$.

results.title: Type of a world
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a Kripke model $M$ and a modal formula $\varphi$, the type (or $\Sigma$-type, for $\Sigma$ the set of subformulas of $\varphi$) of a world $w$ of $M$ is the finite set of subformulas of $\varphi$ that hold at $w$ in $M$.

results.title: Worlds of the filtration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula. The worlds of the filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$ form the finite set of types occurring in $M$: the subsets $s$ of the set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of $\varphi$ such that $s$ is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at some world of $M$.

results.title: Smallest filtration relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world $w$ of $M$ the type of $w$. The smallest filtration relation is the finite set of pairs $(s, t)$ of types such that there are worlds $w$ and $w'$ of $M$ of types $s$ and $t$ with $w'$ accessible from $w$.

results.title: Filtration worlds are realized types
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world $w$ of $M$ the type of $w$. Every world $s$ of the filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$, that is, every element of the finite set of types occurring in $M$, is the type of some world of $M$.

results.title: Worlds of the same type agree on subformulas
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at a world $w$ of $M$ the type of $w$. If two worlds $w$ and $v$ of $M$ have the same type, then every subformula $\psi$ of $\varphi$ holds at $w$ iff it holds at $v$.

results.title: The smallest filtration is a filtration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at a world $w$ the type of $w$. The relation that relates two types when some worlds of those types are related in $M$ is a filtration of $M$ through the set of subformulas of $\varphi$.

results.title: Filtration lemma for the smallest filtration
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\varphi$ a modal formula, and for a world $w$ let $[w]$, the type of $w$, be the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at $w$ in $M$. For every subformula $\psi$ of $\varphi$ and every world $w$ of $M$, $\psi$ holds at $[w]$ in the smallest filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$ iff $\psi$ holds at $w$ in $M$.

results.title: Completeness of K, countermodel form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A modal formula that is not a theorem of K fails at some world of some Kripke model.

results.title: Finite model property of K
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A formula that is not a K-theorem fails in a Kripke model with at most `2 ^ |sub φ|` worlds.

results.title: Finite-check criterion for K-theorems
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of K iff it passes the following finite check: for every nonempty set $U$ of subsets of the set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of $\varphi$, every relation $R \subseteq U \times U$ and every $s \in U$, $\varphi$ evaluates to true at $s$ in the finite Kripke model on $U$ with relation $R$ in which an atom $p$ is true at $s$ iff $p \in s$.

results.title: K-theorems via finite models on sets of subformulas
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of K iff for every nonempty set $U$ of subsets of the set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of $\varphi$ and every finite set $R$ of pairs of finite sets of formulas, $\varphi$ holds at every world of the Kripke model whose worlds are the elements of $U$, in which $s$ sees $t$ iff $(s, t) \in R$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $s$ iff $p \in s$.

results.title: A filtration refutes what the model refutes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\varphi$ a formula and $R$ a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$. If $\varphi$ fails at some world of $M$, then $\varphi$ is not valid in the finite model whose worlds are the types of worlds of $M$ (the sets of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world), with relation $R$ and an atom true at a type iff it belongs to it.

results.title: Lemmon filtration relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a formula, and let $U_\varphi$ be the set of types of worlds of $M$ (the sets of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world). The Lemmon relation is the relation $R$ on $U_\varphi$ such that $s \mathrel{R} t$ iff for every formula $\psi$ with $\Box\psi$ a subformula of $\varphi$, $\Box\psi \in s$ implies $\Box\psi \in t$ and $\psi \in t$.

results.title: S5 filtration relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a formula, and let $U_\varphi$ be the set of types of worlds of $M$ (the sets of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world). The S5 relation is the relation $R$ on $U_\varphi$ such that $s \mathrel{R} t$ iff for every formula $\psi$ with $\Box\psi$ a subformula of $\varphi$, $\Box\psi \in s$ iff $\Box\psi \in t$.

results.title: The Lemmon relation is a filtration of a transitive model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Kripke model $M$ with a transitive accessibility relation and every formula $\varphi$, the Lemmon relation of $M$ and $\varphi$ is a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$.

results.title: The S5 relation is a filtration of an equivalence model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Kripke model $M$ whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and every formula $\varphi$, the S5 relation of $M$ and $\varphi$ is a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$.

results.title: Reflexivity on a finite set of worlds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $U$ be a finite set of finite sets of modal formulas and $R$ a finite set of pairs of such sets. Then $R$ is reflexive on $U$ when $(s, s) \in R$ for every $s \in U$.

results.title: Transitivity on a finite set of worlds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $U$ be a finite set of finite sets of modal formulas and $R$ a finite set of pairs of such sets. Then $R$ is transitive on $U$ when $(s, r) \in R$ for all $s, t, r \in U$ with $(s, t) \in R$ and $(t, r) \in R$.

results.title: Symmetry on a finite set of worlds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $U$ be a finite set of finite sets of modal formulas and $R$ a finite set of pairs of such sets. Then $R$ is symmetric on $U$ when $(t, s) \in R$ for all $s, t \in U$ with $(s, t) \in R$.

results.title: Filtrations of reflexive models are reflexive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive, let $\varphi$ be a modal formula, and let $R$ be a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$. Then $(s, s) \in R$ for every set $s$ that is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at some world of $M$.

results.title: Finite model property of T
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a modal formula $\varphi$ is not a theorem of T, then there is a Kripke model with finitely many worlds, at most $2^{|\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)|}$ of them, where $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, whose accessibility relation is reflexive and in which $\varphi$ is false at some world.

results.title: Finite model property of S4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a modal formula $\varphi$ is not a theorem of S4, then there is a Kripke model with finitely many worlds, at most $2^{|\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)|}$ of them, where $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive and in which $\varphi$ is false at some world.

results.title: Primitive-preserving endomorphism problem for free metabelian groups (Kourovka 14.85)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, posed by E. I. Timoshenko and V. Shpilrain, that for every natural number $n$, every endomorphism $\varphi$ of the free metabelian group $M_n$ of rank $n$ that maps every primitive element of $M_n$ to a primitive element is bijective, hence an automorphism.

results.summary: For every natural number $n$, every endomorphism $\varphi$ of the free metabelian group $M_n$ of rank $n$ that maps every primitive element of $M_n$ to a primitive element is bijective, hence an automorphism of $M_n$. This answers Kourovka Problem 14.85 positively.

results.title: The braid group $B_n$ by Artin's presentation
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the braid group $B_n$ on $n$ strands is the group generated by $\sigma_0, \dots, \sigma_{n-2}$ subject to the relations $\sigma_i \sigma_j = \sigma_j \sigma_i$ for $j \ge i + 2$ and $\sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1}$ for $0 \le i \le n - 3$; it is the trivial group when $n \le 1$.

results.title: Makanin's root-uniqueness question for braid groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and every integer $k \ge 1$, any two elements $\alpha, \beta$ of the braid group $B_n$ on $n$ strands with $\alpha^k = \beta^k$ are conjugate in $B_n$. This is Kourovka Problem 10.23 (G. S. Makanin).

results.title: Roots in braid groups are unique up to conjugacy (González-Meneses)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k \ge 1$, if two elements $\alpha, \beta$ of the braid group $B_n$ on $n$ strands satisfy $\alpha^k = \beta^k$, then $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are conjugate in $B_n$. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.23 (G. S. Makanin) affirmatively.

results.title: The automorphism group of a circular order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a circularly ordered set with non-strict circular betweenness relation $\operatorname{btw}$. The automorphism group of $\alpha$ is the subgroup of the group of permutations of $\alpha$ consisting of the permutations $\sigma$ such that, for all $a, b, c \in \alpha$, $\operatorname{btw}(a, b, c)$ holds if and only if $\operatorname{btw}(\sigma(a), \sigma(b), \sigma(c))$ holds.

results.title: Highly homogeneous permutation groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group of permutations of a set $\alpha$. Then $G$ is highly homogeneous when, for every natural number $k$, it acts transitively on the $k$-element subsets of $\alpha$: for any two $k$-element subsets $X$ and $Y$ of $\alpha$ there is some $g \in G$ with $g(X) = Y$.

results.title: The full symmetric group is highly homogeneous
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $\alpha$, the group of all permutations of $\alpha$ is highly homogeneous: for every natural number $k$, any $k$-element subset of $\alpha$ can be carried to any other $k$-element subset of $\alpha$ by some permutation of $\alpha$.

results.title: Order automorphism group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ equipped with a relation $<$, the order automorphism group of $\alpha$ is the subgroup of the group of permutations of $\alpha$ consisting of the permutations $\sigma$ such that for all $a, b \in \alpha$, $a < b$ holds if and only if $\sigma(a) < \sigma(b)$ holds.

results.title: Spectrum of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The spectrum $\omega(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of orders of its elements, where an element of infinite order is counted as having order $0$.

results.title: Three isospectral finite simple groups
results.caption: Definition

results.title: No three non-isomorphic finite non-abelian simple groups are isospectral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There do not exist three pairwise non-isomorphic finite non-abelian simple groups $G_1, G_2, G_3$ with $\omega(G_1) = \omega(G_2) = \omega(G_3)$, where the spectrum $\omega(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of orders of its elements.

results.summary: For a real place $v$ of a number field $K$, let $\mathfrak m_v$ be the modulus of $K$ with finite part the unit ideal $\mathcal O_K$ and infinite part $\{v\}$. The infinite part of $\mathfrak m_v$ is the singleton $\{v\}$.

results.title: The ray group of a modulus

results.summary: Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The ray group of $\mathfrak m$ is the subgroup of the group of fractional ideals coprime to $\mathfrak m$ generated by the principal ideals $(x)$ of the elements $x \in K^\times$ congruent to $1$ modulo $\mathfrak m$.

results.title: Ray class group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The ray class group of a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$ is the quotient of the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ by the ray group of $\mathfrak m$.

results.title: Ray class map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, the ray class map is the canonical quotient homomorphism from the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ onto the ray class group of $\mathfrak m$, sending each such ideal to its class modulo the ray group of $\mathfrak m$.

results.title: Sign of a unit at a real place
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real place $w$ of a number field $K$, let $\sigma_w \colon K \to \mathbb{R}$ be the corresponding real embedding. results.title: Trivial sign at a real place means positivity
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Trivial infinite sign means positivity at the modulus
results.caption: Theorem

For every ray element $x$ of $m$, the infinite sign map of $m$ sends $x$ to the identity if and only if $x$ is positive at the infinite part of $m$, that is, $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.

results.title: Ray elements positive at the infinite part
results.caption: Definition

The positive ray elements of $m$ form the subgroup of the ray elements of $m$ defined as the kernel of the infinite sign map of $m$; equivalently, they are the ray elements $x$ with $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.

results.title: Membership in the positive ray elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ with finite set of real places $m_\infty$, and for a real place $w$ let $\sigma_w$ be the real embedding of $K$ at $w$. A ray element $x$ of $m$ is a positive ray element of $m$ if and only if $x$ is positive at the infinite part of $m$, that is, $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.

results.title: Residue-sign map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The residue-sign map of $m$ is the group homomorphism from the ray elements of $m$ to the residue-sign target of $m$ that sends a ray element $x$ to the pair formed by the image of $x$ under the infinite sign map of $m$ and the image of $x$ under the finite residue map of $m$.

results.title: Components of the residue-sign map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. For every ray element $x$ of $m$, the image of $x$ under the residue-sign map of $m$ is the pair whose first component is the image of $x$ under the infinite sign map of $m$ and whose second component is the image of $x$ under the finite residue map of $m$.

results.title: Ray-one subgroup
results.caption: Definition

The ray-one subgroup of $m$ is the subgroup of the ray elements of $m$ consisting of the ray elements $x$ that lie in the finite ray-one subgroup of $m$ (those congruent to $1$ at the finite part of $m$) and in the subgroup of ray elements positive at every real place in the infinite part of $m$.

results.title: Membership in the ray-one subgroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. A ray element $x$ of $m$ lies in the ray-one subgroup of $m$ if and only if $x$ is congruent to $1$ at the finite part of $m$ and $x$ is positive at every real place in the infinite part of $m$.

results.title: Surjectivity of the residue-sign map
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Kernel of the residue-sign map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The kernel of the residue-sign map of $m$ is the ray-one subgroup of $m$.

results.title: Kernel criterion for the residue-sign map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. A ray element $x$ of $m$ is sent to $1$ by the residue-sign map of $m$ if and only if $x$ is a ray element congruent to $1$ modulo $m$: $x$ is a ray element of $m$, $x$ is congruent to $1$ at the finite part of $m$, and $x$ is positive at every real place in the infinite part of $m$.

results.title: The residue-sign isomorphism
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The residue-sign isomorphism of $m$ is the group isomorphism from the quotient of the ray elements of $m$ by the ray-one subgroup of $m$ onto the residue-sign target of $m$ induced by the residue-sign map, which is surjective with kernel the ray-one subgroup; it sends the class of a ray element $x$ to the image of $x$ under the residue-sign map.

results.title: The residue-sign isomorphism on classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. For every ray element $x$ of $m$, the residue-sign isomorphism of $m$ sends the class of $x$ in the quotient of the ray elements of $m$ by the ray-one subgroup to the image of $x$ under the residue-sign map of $m$.

results.title: Digits of a p-adic integer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. The $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$ is the natural number $(a_{n+1} - a_n)/p^n$.

results.title: p-adic digits measure the gaps between approximations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th $p$-adic digit $d_n$ of $a$ satisfies $d_n p^n = a_{n+1} - a_n$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. results.title: Reduced forms of a given discriminant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $d$, $R(d)$ is the finite set of integer triples $(a, b, c)$ such that the binary quadratic form $a x^2 + b x y + c y^2$ is Gauss reduced (that is, $a > 0$, $b^2 - 4ac < 0$, $|b| \le a \le c$, and $b \ge 0$ whenever $|b| = a$ or $a = c$) and has discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = d$. In particular $R(d)$ is empty when $d \ge 0$.

results.title: Gauss class number of a discriminant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $d$, the Gauss class number $h(d)$ is the number of integer triples $(a, b, c)$ with $b^2 - 4ac = d$ for which the binary quadratic form $ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$ is positive definite ($a > 0$ and $d < 0$), reduced ($|b| \le a \le c$, with $b \ge 0$ whenever $|b| = a$ or $a = c$) and primitive ($\gcd(a, b, c) = 1$).

results.title: Unweighted Hurwitz class number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $d$, the unweighted Hurwitz class number $H(d)$ is the number of elements of the set $R(d)$ of reduced forms of discriminant $d$, that is, the number of integer triples $(a, b, c)$, primitive or not, for which $a x^2 + b x y + c y^2$ is a Gauss-reduced binary quadratic form of discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = d$. Every reduced form is counted with weight $1$; in particular $H(d) = 0$ when $d \ge 0$.

results.title: Weight of a reduced binary quadratic form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weight of an integer triple $(a, b, c)$, standing for the form $ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$, is $1/2$ if $a = c$ and $b = 0$, $1/3$ if $a = b = c \ne 0$, and $1$ otherwise.

results.title: Kronecker's sum $F_o(n)$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $F_o(n)$ is the sum of the weights of the reduced positive-definite integral binary quadratic forms $ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$ of discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = -4n$ in which $a$ or $c$ is odd. Here a form is reduced when $|b| \le a \le c$, with $b \ge 0$ whenever $|b| = a$ or $a = c$, and its weight is $1/2$ if $a = c$ and $b = 0$, $1/3$ if $a = b = c$, and $1$ otherwise.

results.title: Instances of MAXIMUM CUT
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of MAXIMUM CUT is a triple $(n, E, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a finite list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers (the edges) and a natural number $K$ (the bound).

results.title: Well-formed MAXIMUM CUT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of MAXIMUM CUT is well formed when the list $E$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and the reversed pair $(v, u)$ does not occur in $E$.

results.title: Feasible MAXIMUM CUT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(n, E, K)$ of MAXIMUM CUT is feasible when there are a finite set $S$ of natural numbers, all less than $n$, and a list $C$ of length at least $K$ obtained from $E$ by deleting zero or more of its entries, such that every pair $(u, v)$ in $C$ has exactly one of $u$ and $v$ in $S$.

results.title: MAXIMUM CUT as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM CUT accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when decoding $x$ with the canonical bitstring encoding of instances of MAXIMUM CUT succeeds and yields an instance that is well formed and feasible. All other bitstrings, including those that fail to decode, are rejected.
